slides.heading: The <accent>Announcement</accent>
slides.caption: Claude Code just released Auto Mode -- a smarter way to handle permissions

slides.heading: The <accent>Problem</accent>
before: Ask Before Edits = stops every few seconds
You can't walk away from long tasks
after: Claude can delete files, run anything

slides.heading: What <accent>Ask Mode</accent> Looks Like
slides.caption: Every edit, every bash command -- Claude stops and waits for your approval

slides.heading: Enter <accent>Auto Mode</accent>
slides.body:
- A classifier checks each action before executing
- Safe actions run automatically
- Risky actions get flagged and blocked
- Claude tries a different approach if blocked
- Ideal for long-running tasks

slides.heading: Auto Mode <accent>In Action</accent>
slides.caption: Notice 'Auto mode' in the bottom bar -- Claude handles permissions intelligently

slides.heading: Risky Actions Get <accent>Flagged</accent>
slides.caption: Tried to delete files -- Auto Mode caught it and asked for confirmation

slides.heading: How to <accent>Enable</accent> It
slides.body:
- Available for Claude Team plans now
- Enterprise + API coming soon
- Works in terminal and VS Code
- Toggle via Shift+Tab in CLI

terminal.text: Claude will make changes without asking.

slides.heading: <accent>Official</accent> Announcement
slides.caption: Anthropic's blog -- Auto mode sits between 'ask everything' and 'skip everything'

slides.heading: Key <accent>Takeaways</accent>
items: Auto Mode = smart middle ground for permissions
Classifier checks every tool call for risk
Safe actions run, risky ones get blocked
Sessions cost slightly more (AI reviews each action)
Best for long-running tasks you want to walk away from
